questions.question: List the main parts of a coal-fired power station in order and state the energy transfer at each stage.
questions.expected_answer: Boiler: chemical potential energy in coal → thermal energy, which turns water into high-pressure steam. Turbine: thermal energy of steam → kinetic energy of the spinning shaft. Generator: kinetic energy → electrical energy (a rotating magnet in coils). Condenser/cooling tower: remaining heat transferred to the surroundings; water reused.

questions.question: A power station releases 600 MJ of chemical energy from coal and produces 200 MJ of electrical energy. Calculate its efficiency and state what happens to the rest of the energy.
questions.expected_answer: Efficiency = useful energy out ÷ energy in = 200 ÷ 600 = 1/3, about 33%. The remaining 400 MJ is transferred to the surroundings as heat (hot flue gases, cooling water, friction), not destroyed.

questions.question: Give three environmental effects of generating electricity from coal.
questions.expected_answer: Carbon dioxide emissions contribute to global warming and climate change; sulfur dioxide forms acid rain; fly ash and soot pollute the air and harm health; coal mining scars land and causes acid mine drainage; large amounts of water are used; ash dumps must be stored.
